title: Illustration / Tips and techniques

location.series: IBM Design Language / public web guidelines
location.extent: Complete webpage content-area capture; interactive elements retain their captured state

slide_intent: Decide what an illustration must explain and where it will appear before choosing detail, color and composition, so its emphasis supports the viewer’s task.
strategic_value: Deliberate differences between hero and supporting imagery can preserve IBM’s visual character while protecting functional focal points.
demonstration: The page compares abstract/literal, micro/macro and low/high-fidelity images, then pairs hero and supporting applications with color, contrast, canvas and composition guidance.
practical_value: Choose an illustration’s explanatory role first, then set its scale, fidelity, palette and focal point for that role.

content_islands.name: Ways of seeing
content_islands.spec: Compare an abstract green image with a literal laptop, a close-up eye with a city view, and linework with shaded layers.

content_islands.name: Featured and supportive roles
content_islands.spec: Show a brochure-like hero application above a supporting illustration in a screen layout.

content_islands.name: Color choices
content_islands.spec: Follow a large purple illustration with monochromatic, analogous and complementary examples, then blue-focus and additional-color comparisons.

content_islands.name: Accessibility and canvas
content_islands.spec: Compare readable and unreadable line imagery before the nested aspect-ratio diagram.

content_islands.name: Composition
content_islands.spec: Close with two-sided and horizon framing diagrams and focal-point compositions paired with 2x Grid overlays.

ingredient.name: Featured versus supportive illustration
ingredient.role: Give an idea the right amount of attention without competing with its surrounding content.
ingredient.application: Use more intricate imagery for a featured story; simplify supporting illustrations for quick recognition and maintain clear separation from functional focal points.
ingredient.scope: Illustration guidance for the described IBM contexts. Accessibility requirements concern information not fully conveyed in accompanying text; platform-specific canvas requirements may override common aspect ratios.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source explains how intent sets the decision framework and how color reinforces expression without obscuring important UI elements.
reference_purposes.Expression: Comparisons show multiple ways IBM illustration handles abstraction, scale, fidelity and color.
reference_purposes.Application: Hero/spot examples and grid diagrams teach selection of complexity and placement.
reference_purposes.Constraint: The source limits additional colors to specific needs, warns against competing with blue UI actions, and requires 3:1 contrast for key informational concepts not fully supplied in adjacent text.
